Sort-mode macro cache compatibility adaptation — 2026-11-27

The three JavaScript edits in citeproc-sort-macro-cache.json are derived from
citeproc-js by Frank Bennett (Copyright (c) 2009-2019 Frank Bennett). The
sort-mode cache change is contributed by Dan Stillman in upstream PR276:
https://github.com/Juris-M/citeproc-js/pull/276
Pinned source revision: adffcfa3189ed21cbdb5272a74a8edbf817ac326
Pinned source file: src/util_nodes.js
SHA-256 of the upstream GitHub unified patch text (without a trailing newline):
d811d34432150559e80bd338650456b3d592cca03474b77bbc09e818b8cc2703

This is an unmerged upstream compatibility patch, not an official citeproc-js
release. It is applied by carr-academic-runtime/1 only in memory after checking
the exact original processor and the complete local patch asset. The three
edits emit a sort-macro call, cache that macro separately from display macros,
and configure its token list. No style, locale or original processor file is
rewritten. The original CPAL and AGPL license copies and NOTICE remain here.
This adaptation selects CPAL-1.0, as the original distribution does.

The contents of the covered JavaScript edits are subject to the Common Public
Attribution License Version 1.0 (the "License"); you may not use them except
in compliance with the License. A copy accompanies them in
LICENSE-CPAL-1.0.txt and is available at https://opensource.org/license/cpal_1-0.
The License is based on the Mozilla Public License Version 1.1, with Sections
14 and 15 for network use and attribution. The Original Code is citeproc-js.
The Initial Developer of the Original Code is Frank Bennett. Portions written
by Frank Bennett are Copyright (c) 2009-2019 Frank Bennett. All Rights Reserved.
The software is supplied without warranty; see the accompanying full License.

The human-readable exact before/after edits, original source, adapter source,
and licenses are shipped together. Every new citation document names the
original processor plus this separate adapter's resource profile, patch hash,
source revision, original/derived processor hashes and attribution. Original
receipts continue to be recognized exactly; explicit regeneration produces a
new document naming the adapter and leaves the old file unchanged.
